tagline: A web of back roads below the Catskill escarpment.
intro: This byway is a web rather than a line, twenty-one miles of town and county roads crossing the Durham Valley, which slopes from the northernmost escarpment of the Catskills to a plain rolling gently north toward Albany and east to the Hudson. The state first marked them as scenic roads in 1991.

Old houses, farms, stone bridges and stone walls stand along the way. From one point the Five State View runs out over the Hudson Valley to the Berkshires, Vermont, Connecticut and New Hampshire, and north to the Adirondacks.

moments.title: East Durham
moments.text: A hamlet known for its Irish heritage, where the stone arch bridge on Woodward Road is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

moments.title: Durham
moments.text: The town took the name of Durham, Connecticut, in 1805, after years of being called New Durham by its many settlers from Connecticut.
